faq.q: How did countries fix the ozone hole?
faq.a: In the 1987 Montreal Protocol, countries agreed to phase out chemicals called CFCs used in fridges and sprays. Every UN member joined, and the ozone layer is expected to recover around the middle of this century.
A trade bloc is a group of countries that agree to cut taxes and barriers on trade between them, like ASEAN, the EU, Mercosur in South America or the African Continental Free Trade Area.
asks: What is a free trade area?

faq.a: A treaty is a formal written agreement between countries. Once a country ratifies it, which means officially approves it, it promises to follow it.
Through the Universal Postal Union, set up in 1874 in Bern, Switzerland. Its member countries agree to deliver each other's mail, so one stamp can send a letter around the world.
asks: What is the Universal Postal Union?

faq.q: Do countries always keep international agreements?
faq.a: Not always. Some agreements have no strong way to force countries to obey, and countries sometimes leave them. Others, like the Montreal Protocol, have worked very well.
asks: Can a country break a treaty?

facts: The Montreal Protocol (1987) became the first treaty in UN history to be ratified by every UN member state.
The Universal Postal Union was founded in 1874 in Bern, Switzerland.
